Uptime in 49 seconds

One monitor: status, coverage and recent checks
Add a monitor from a website address
A scheduled job watched and recovered

run-uptime.com
↗
GitHub
→

Uptime watches your websites and APIs on a schedule and tells you only when a failure is confirmed. It never calls a missing check healthy, and it keeps the evidence behind every incident. Alerts go to email, Slack or a signed webhook.

What it does
Check web pages and API responses for the right status, text, headers, data values and speed
Check that a server port answers, that DNS records are right, and that SSL certificates and domain registrations are not about to expire
Choose how many failed checks in a row open an incident and how many passes close it
Show a time as Unknown when no check arrived, instead of guessing it was fine
Watch cron jobs and nightly backups through heartbeat check-ins
Alert you by email, Slack or a signed webhook, and run an alert drill to learn whether a message really reaches someone
Pause alerts during planned maintenance windows
Run checks from a machine on your own network and export your monitors, evidence and alert history any time
What it promises
One failed check never raises an alarm. A monitor is called Failing only after confirmation, a missing check shows as Unknown, and it recovers only on fresh passing checks.
Every scheduled check and every retry is kept with its time, result and error type, and a retry never erases an earlier failure.
Only confirmed incident changes send automatic alerts, and a test send never changes a monitor's status.
Planned and recurring maintenance windows use US time zones and daylight saving, and keep the underlying check results so reports still show what happened.
Each alert gets one automatic send per destination where a repeat could double up, an unclear outcome is not sent again, and 'accepted' is never reported as 'read'.
An alert drill sends a clearly marked test with a one-time confirmation link, and a confirmation is the recipient's own report, never proof of monitoring.
Certificate checks look at trust, host name and expiry from each location, warn in stages before a certificate runs out, and clear only after a new valid certificate is seen.
A backup restores only into an empty installation: monitors come back paused, destinations disabled and old alerts held back.
Every address and redirect is validated, unsafe addresses are refused, and a redirect that downgrades from HTTPS is rejected.
An owner can erase a monitor with its evidence, an alert destination, or an operator, and gets a receipt of what was removed.

Attention: what needs you next

run-nook.com
↗

Nook is a team chat where a message can become a decision or a request, and everyone can see who is on it. It has public, private and direct channels with threads, one list of what needs you, and quiet time when you need to focus. You can keep Slack running while your team tries it.

What it does
Talk in public channels, private channels and direct messages, with replies kept in threads and emoji reactions
Turn a message into a recorded decision or a request that only the person asked can accept
See requests for you, mentions and replies you follow in one list, and go quiet for an hour when you need to focus
Attach images, PDFs and text files to messages, kept private to the conversation
Search any message you are allowed to read, and set reminders or schedule messages for later
Invite teammates and choose which channels each person sees
Opt in to email and phone notifications for mentions and urgent requests
Bring in your Slack history as read-only channels, and back everything up to one file you can restore later
What it promises
Every action checks who you are and whether you are in that conversation; workspace admins cannot read other people's direct messages.
A message is saved once however many times a send is retried, and edits never overwrite a newer version.
A request becomes accepted only through the person it was assigned to, and a completed item is reported as completed, never as verified.
Muting hides routine updates but never an explicit mention or a request to you.
Removing someone from a channel cuts their reading, writing and search access immediately. New members can see a channel's whole history.
If a request's wording or deadline materially changes, the assignee must accept the new version again.
Email is off for everyone until they turn it on, goes only to your own sign-in address, and covers only mentions, urgent requests and commitments.
Attachments are kept private and are checked for membership on every download; only text, PNG, JPEG and PDF files are accepted.
Backups include every conversation, decision, file and attention choice with integrity checks, and leave out live sign-ins.
Owners and admins can erase messages and members, but never the last owner, and never through a door into private direct messages.

Check web pages and API responses for the right status, text, headers, data values and speed
Check that a server port answers, that DNS records are right, and that SSL certificates and domain registrations are not about to expire

One failed check never raises an alarm. A monitor is called Failing only after confirmation, a missing check shows as Unknown, and it recovers only on fresh passing checks.
Every scheduled check and every retry is kept with its time, result and error type, and a retry never erases an earlier failure.
Only confirmed incident changes send automatic alerts, and a test send never changes a monitor's status.

Certificate checks look at trust, host name and expiry from each location, warn in stages before a certificate runs out, and clear only after a new valid certificate is seen.
A backup restores only into an empty installation: monitors come back paused, destinations disabled and old alerts held back.

What it does
Talk in public channels, private channels and direct messages, with replies kept in threads and emoji reactions
Turn a message into a recorded decision or a request that only the person asked can accept
See requests for you, mentions and replies you follow in one list, and go quiet for an hour when you need to focus
Attach images, PDFs and text files to messages, kept private to the conversation
Search any message you are allowed to read, and set reminders or schedule messages for later
Invite teammates and choose which channels each person sees
Opt in to email and phone notifications for mentions and urgent requests
Bring in your Slack history as read-only channels, and back everything up to one file you can restore later
What it promises
Every action checks who you are and whether you are in that conversation; workspace admins cannot read other people's direct messages.
A message is saved once however many times a send is retried, and edits never overwrite a newer version.
A request becomes accepted only through the person it was assigned to, and a completed item is reported as completed, never as verified.
Muting hides routine updates but never an explicit mention or a request to you.
Removing someone from a channel cuts their reading, writing and search access immediately. New members can see a channel's whole history.
If a request's wording or deadline materially changes, the assignee must accept the new version again.
Email is off for everyone until they turn it on, goes only to your own sign-in address, and covers only mentions, urgent requests and commitments.
Attachments are kept private and are checked for membership on every download; only text, PNG, JPEG and PDF files are accepted.
Backups include every conversation, decision, file and attention choice with integrity checks, and leave out live sign-ins.
Owners and admins can erase messages and members, but never the last owner, and never through a door into private direct messages.

↗
GitHub
→

Uptime watches your websites and APIs on a schedule and tells you only when a failure is confirmed. It never calls a missing check healthy, and it keeps the evidence behind every incident. Alerts go to email, Slack or a signed webhook.

What it does
Check web pages and API responses for the right status, text, headers, data values and speed
Check that a server port answers, that DNS records are right, and that SSL certificates and domain registrations are not about to expire
Choose how many failed checks in a row open an incident and how many passes close it
Show a time as Unknown when no check arrived, instead of guessing it was fine
Watch cron jobs and nightly backups through heartbeat check-ins
Alert you by email, Slack or a signed webhook, and run an alert drill to learn whether a message really reaches someone
Pause alerts during planned maintenance windows
Run checks from a machine on your own network and export your monitors, evidence and alert history any time
What it promises
One failed check never raises an alarm. A monitor is called Failing only after confirmation, a missing check shows as Unknown, and it recovers only on fresh passing checks.
Every scheduled check and every retry is kept with its time, result and error type, and a retry never erases an earlier failure.
Only confirmed incident changes send automatic alerts, and a test send never changes a monitor's status.
Planned and recurring maintenance windows use US time zones and daylight saving, and keep the underlying check results so reports still show what happened.
Each alert gets one automatic send per destination where a repeat could double up, an unclear outcome is not sent again, and 'accepted' is never reported as 'read'.
An alert drill sends a clearly marked test with a one-time confirmation link, and a confirmation is the recipient's own report, never proof of monitoring.
Certificate checks look at trust, host name and expiry from each location, warn in stages before a certificate runs out, and clear only after a new valid certificate is seen.
A backup restores only into an empty installation: monitors come back paused, destinations disabled and old alerts held back.
Every address and redirect is validated, unsafe addresses are refused, and a redirect that downgrades from HTTPS is rejected.
An owner can erase a monitor with its evidence, an alert destination, or an operator, and gets a receipt of what was removed.
